package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects 'Wallpapers Blur HD' and 'Booster & Cleaner Pro' as distributed at time of discovery)
package_info.why_malicious: The applications contain embedded ransomware code that abuses granted permissions to harvest personal data from the victim's device, exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled servers, and then extorts the user by threatening to leak the data unless a ransom is paid. This constitutes a severe violation of user privacy, device security, and trust.

execution_context.trigger: on app launch after permissions are granted
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (Java/Android), typically within the main Activity or a background Service

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after permissions are granted, the code collects personal data from the device (contacts, photos, messages), uploads the harvested data to a remote attacker-controlled server via the internet, and then displays a ransom note threatening to leak the data unless payment is made.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically harvests sensitive user data (contacts, photos, SMS) and exfiltrates it to an external server without user consent, then displays a ransom note demanding payment under threat of data exposure. This combination of unauthorized data exfiltration and extortion is characteristic of ransomware and is never legitimate in consumer apps.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not collect and transmit personal data without explicit, informed user consent, nor do they threaten users with exposure of their data. Displaying a ransom note and demanding payment is a clear violation of user trust and platform policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or cloud sync applications may collect and upload user data, but only with explicit user consent, transparent privacy policies, and never with threats or extortion. Such apps also typically use secure, well-known endpoints and provide opt-out mechanisms.
key_indicators: Bulk access to contacts, photos, and SMS messages immediately after permissions are granted
Automated upload of harvested data to remote servers not associated with the app's stated function
Display of a ransom or extortion message referencing the user's own data
Use of excessive permissions unrelated to the app's advertised purpose

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly benign app (e.g., 'Wallpapers Blur HD' or 'Booster & Cleaner Pro') from Google Play.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is granted permissions to access personal data (contacts, photos, SMS, camera, internet).

attack_chain.action: After permissions are granted, the malicious code executes and harvests personal data from the device, including contacts, photos, and SMS messages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Harvested data is uploaded to attacker-controlled servers.

attack_chain.action: The app displays a ransom note to the user, threatening to leak the harvested data unless a ransom is paid.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is extorted for payment; attacker's objective is achieved if ransom is paid.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected collection and exfiltration of personal data (contacts, photos, SMS) by non-backup or non-messaging apps
Display of ransom or extortion messages referencing the user's own data and threatening exposure
Network connections to unknown or suspicious servers immediately following data collection
file_indicators: Android apps requesting excessive permissions (READ_CONTACTS, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, READ_SMS, CAMERA, INTERNET) not justified by app description
Presence of code accessing contacts, photos, SMS, and uploading data to remote endpoints
Inclusion of hardcoded URLs or IP addresses not associated with legitimate cloud providers
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs after data collection events
Unusual data upload patterns (large or bulk data transfers) from apps not expected to sync or backup data
Connections to domains or IPs not listed in the app's privacy policy or documentation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android applications for requests of excessive permissions relative to their stated purpose. Use dynamic analysis to detect runtime behaviors involving bulk access to personal data followed by outbound network connections to unknown servers. Flag apps that display ransom notes or extortion messages referencing user data. Employ network monitoring to identify suspicious data uploads from apps not expected to transmit user data, and correlate with app permission requests and user interface actions.
